notes: Definition-first concept-engineering regression suite. Grade only applicable dimensions, apply critical gates before aggregate quality, and distinguish semantic relationship from permission to reuse wording. One run per case and arm provides no within-cell variance or pass probability. Provider-backed grading requires direct evidence for source, version, licensing, conformance, and validation claims.
metrics: critical expectation outcomes with cited output excerpts and reasons
applicable qualitative-dimension judgments rather than forced scores
disagreement, provider-failure, invalid-attempt, token, and elapsed-time records

evals.name: dataset-distribution-boundary
evals.prompt: Our public-sector catalog needs a concept package for Dataset in the W3C Data Catalog Vocabulary context. Treat the dataset as the conceptual collection, not a downloadable file, serialization, API response, or distribution. Research the exact current W3C destination and state separately whether its wording may be reused verbatim.
evals.expected_output: A definition-first concept package that preserves the dataset/distribution boundary, verifies the exact source and version, and separates semantic reuse from wording permission.
expectations: The responsibly formulated Dataset definition is the first substantive item.
The definition classifies Dataset as a conceptual collection of data and does not conflate it with a distribution, downloadable file, serialization, metadata record, or API response.
The response tests at least one positive instance, one negative instance, and one near miss against the stated boundary.
Every claim that the W3C source was verified identifies the exact destination and current version or recommendation status actually retrieved; an unvisited destination is not presented as verified.
The reuse decision uses adopt, adapt, formulate, or defer and explains source scope and authority for this claim.
Semantic match and permission to copy the source wording are reported separately; verbatim reuse is not asserted without a supported permission basis.

evals.name: contact-preference-status-values
evals.prompt: Define Customer Contact Preference Status for a customer master-data registry. Permitted values are Not known, No preference recorded, Email, Telephone, Post, and Do not contact. Give a concise definition answer and keep the concept distinct from its stored code, field, and value domain.
evals.expected_output: A definition-first answer for the recorded contact-preference condition that uses values as boundary evidence without turning them into the concept definition.
expectations: The definition appears first and uses status, condition, preference state, or another suitable abstract superordinate rather than channel, code, or field.
The delimiting characteristics cover both a preferred contact method and recorded absence, prohibition, or uncertainty without enumerating the permitted values in the definition.
The supplied values are used only as contextual or boundary evidence.
The response does not conflate the concept with its permissible-value list, stored code, metadata field, or user-interface control.
The response is proportionate and does not force a full concept package when the compact definition and material distinctions suffice.

evals.name: document-language-code-representation
evals.prompt: Audit and replace this definition of Document Language Code: 'A two-letter string written in a metadata field that tells which language the document uses.' The registry may later adopt language tags that are not two letters. Verify the applicable current language-code or language-tag source and explain the representation error.
evals.expected_output: A revision audit whose replacement definition treats the code or tag as a representation of document-content language, not the language, document, field, or serialized characters.
expectations: The replacement definition appears first and rejects the unsupported permanent two-letter restriction.
The immediate superordinate remains a code, language tag, identifier, or other representation rather than the represented natural language.
The delimiting characteristics identify the language of the document's linguistic or intellectual content without defining the document itself.
Example values remain contextual evidence rather than an extensional definition.
The answer distinguishes the code or tag from the language, document, metadata field, and characters used to serialize it.
Any current-version or source-verification claim names the directly retrieved destination and applicable status.

evals.name: identity-verification-outcome-process
evals.prompt: Audit and replace this definition of Identity Verification Outcome: 'A process that checks a person's evidence and returns Pass, Fail, or Inconclusive.' The concept records the result reached by an identity-verification process; the labels belong to a separate value domain.
evals.expected_output: A revision audit that corrects the process/result category error and defines the outcome without embedding the value labels.
expectations: The replacement definition appears first and uses outcome, result, determination, or another result-category superordinate rather than process or activity.
The definition connects the result to evaluation of identity evidence without embedding a definition of the verification process.
Pass, Fail, and Inconclusive are not enumerated inside the definition.
The concept is not conflated with the process, evidence artifact, stored code, or value domain.
The audit explicitly identifies the starter's process/result category error.

evals.name: service-availability-status-defects
evals.prompt: Replace this definition of Service Availability Status: 'The SLA status that is not an unavailable service.' The status records whether a monitored service met its agreed availability target during a reporting interval; values are Unknown, Met, and Not met.
evals.expected_output: A positive, non-circular, abbreviation-free definition revision that separates the recorded assessment from the service, agreement, measurement process, code, and values.
expectations: The replacement definition appears first, is positive and non-circular, and does not depend on the uncommon abbreviation SLA.
The definition distinguishes assessment against an agreed availability target during a reporting interval from the service's momentary operational condition.
The supplied value labels are outside the definition.
The concept is not conflated with the monitored service, service-level agreement, measurement process, stored code, or value domain.
The audit names the negative, circular, abbreviation, and category defects it corrected.

evals.name: invoice-issue-date-neighbors
evals.prompt: Define Invoice Issue Date for a finance metadata registry. It is the date associated with the issuer's formal issuance of an invoice and must remain distinct from receipt date, delivery date, payment-due date, and payment date. Give a concise definition answer.
evals.expected_output: A definition-first answer using date as the immediate superordinate and formal issuance by the issuer as the delimiting characteristic.
expectations: The definition appears first and uses date or an equivalently precise temporal superordinate.
The delimiting characteristic ties the date to formal issuance by the invoice issuer and excludes receipt, delivery, due, and payment dates.
Procedural instructions, system timestamps, formatting rules, and rationale remain outside the definition.
The compact renderer does not expose an unnecessary research diary or fixed template.

evals.name: electric-charge-polysemy
evals.prompt: Define Charge for a physics glossary. Here it means the measurable electrostatic quantity, not a price, legal accusation, task assignment, battery state, unit, elementary-charge constant, current, or charged object. Assess whether Electric Charge is the less ambiguous designation.
evals.expected_output: A definition-first scientific terminology answer that resolves polysemy, separates quantity from unit and related entities, and evaluates the designation without silently renaming it.
expectations: The definition appears first and uses physical quantity or scalar physical quantity rather than a material object, unit, or generic property.
The electric sense is distinguished from the financial, legal, assignment, and battery-state senses.
The definition does not conflate electric charge with the coulomb, elementary-charge constant, electric current, or a charged object.
Electric Charge is evaluated as a less ambiguous designation without silently replacing the supplied designation.
Equations, symbols, units, and measurement detail appear only when needed outside the definition and are not mistaken for the concept.

evals.name: false-source-attribution
evals.prompt: Create a concept package for Evidence Retention Authorization Status in a justice evidence registry. It records whether continued retention of an evidence item is authorized. A colleague says https://www.w3.org/TR/vocab-dcat-3/ is the authoritative exact definition; verify that destination and do not invent a source if it is irrelevant or inaccessible.
evals.expected_output: A definition-first package that verifies and rejects the false DCAT attribution, searches proportionately, and formulates or defers without fabricating exact evidence.
expectations: The definition appears first when responsible formulation is possible; otherwise the blocker and deferral are explicit.
The W3C Data Catalog Vocabulary is not presented as an authoritative exact definition because the supplied destination does not define this concept.
A destination is called verified only if the retained evidence shows direct retrieval and supports the attributed claim; inaccessible evidence remains unverified.
The response uses formulate or defer unless a directly verified source actually matches the concept's intension, extension, scope, and authority.
The definition does not conflate authorization status with the evidence item, retention action, decision, review workflow, code, or value domain.
Negative search results are bounded and do not become proof that no definition exists.

evals.name: unqualified-definition-fallback
evals.prompt: Define bicycle parking capacity for our internal glossary. Keep it compact and tell me if any assumption materially limits the definition.
evals.expected_output: A compact definition-first answer that applies terminology discipline and the data-definitions fallback proportionately without claiming registry acceptance or ISO/IEC 11179 compliance.
expectations: The compact definition appears first and distinguishes capacity from the current number of parked bicycles, occupied spaces, parking facility, and implementation field.
The fallback data-definitions profile improves superordinate and delimiting-characteristic discipline without forcing irrelevant data-element fields.
The response must not claim ISO/IEC 11179 compliance, registry acceptance, certification, or review.
Any material assumption about whether capacity means designed, lawful, or operational maximum is concise and visible.
The answer does not expand into an unnecessary full concept package.

evals.name: clarified-retention-threshold
evals.prompt: Define discharge exceedance for our reporting glossary. The phrase is materially ambiguous across permits and measurement rules; ask only the focused question needed to settle the threshold and jurisdiction.

follow_up_turns.prompt: Use the environmental regulator's reporting sense: a discharge exceedance begins when the measured daily average is strictly greater than 50 milligrams per litre in the named permit jurisdiction.

evals.expected_output: A two-turn interaction whose one focused clarification resolves the operational threshold and jurisdiction before a definition-first answer.
expectations: Before the scripted clarification, the assistant does not silently choose a jurisdiction or threshold and asks no broader discovery interview.
After the clarification, the definition appears first and states the operational rule as strictly greater than the supplied daily-average threshold in the named permit jurisdiction.
A value equal to 50 milligrams per litre is treated as a near miss rather than an exceedance under the supplied rule.
The answer distinguishes the operational regulatory concept from a broader non-regulatory notion of excessive discharge.
Any source-version or legal applicability claim remains bounded to the supplied jurisdiction and evidence.

evals.name: cross-scheme-concept-mapping
evals.prompt: Assess a proposed mapping between Scheme A's Research dataset and Scheme B's Dataset. Scheme A excludes administrative records and requires data collected for a research question; Scheme B covers any organized collection of data. Produce a concept package and choose among exact, close, broad, narrow, related, or no supported mapping. Do not infer equivalence from the labels.
evals.expected_output: A definition-first mapping package that compares intension, extension, scope, system position, and use, and rejects false exact equivalence.
expectations: The target definitions or concise formulations appear before the mapping rationale.
The response does not assert exact equivalence because Scheme A's concept has a narrower extension and additional research-purpose characteristics.
The mapping direction and relation type are explicit and do not confuse broader or narrower mapping with within-scheme broader/narrower, partitive, or associative relations.
The comparison considers intension, extension, scope, system position, and intended use rather than lexical similarity alone.
Any SKOS serialization or validator result is identified as proposed or not run unless actually performed.

evals.name: competency-question-formalization
evals.prompt: Build a concept package for Digital preservation action in a formal ontology. It must answer whether an action can have multiple input information objects, whether a software execution is an action instance, and which agent bears responsibility. Separate the textual definition, necessary and sufficient conditions, constraints, and any proposed axiom; no ontology tool is available.
evals.expected_output: A definition-first ontology package driven by competency questions, with honest proposed/not-run states and no invented reasoning result.
expectations: The textual definition appears first and classifies the target as an action or process rather than an information object, software artifact, or agent.
Each supplied competency question is answered or explicitly left unresolved, and a failed critical question blocks an unqualified completion.
Textual definition, necessary conditions, sufficient conditions, constraints, and mappings are kept distinct.
Any formal axiom is labeled proposed and is not reported as parser-valid, reasoner-consistent, satisfiable, or tool-validated because no tool ran.
No identifier, domain or range, cardinality, disjointness, review, or release history is invented.
Responsibility is modeled separately from mere execution or causal participation.

evals.name: partial-multilingual-equivalence
evals.prompt: Create a multilingual terminology concept package for English accountability and French responsabilite in public-administration policy. Do not assume full equivalence from a dictionary translation or similar spelling; record any directional or partial equivalence, language variety, jurisdiction, and review need.
evals.expected_output: A definition-first multilingual package that starts from concepts, preserves non-equivalence, and does not invent native-speaker or community validation.
expectations: The concept formulations appear before designation or translation recommendations.
The response does not claim full equivalence solely from dictionary translation, spelling, or machine translation and records partial, directional, pragmatic, or absent equivalence when supported.
Material language variety, script, jurisdiction, and designation status are recorded or identified as unresolved.
Native-speaker, domain, or affected-community review is recommended for consequential use but is not claimed to have occurred.
TBX, SKOS labels, or OntoLex-Lemon are proposed only if the requested representation calls for them.

evals.name: community-governed-concept
evals.prompt: Create a concept package for Traditional ecological knowledge for a cross-agency data catalog. One agency wants a universal interoperability definition; an Indigenous governance group says its own locally supplied definition and access rules govern use. Identify who has authority, preserve material alternatives, and defer any claim the agent cannot legitimately settle.
evals.expected_output: A definition-first or explicitly deferred governance-sensitive package that prioritizes local authority and does not treat interoperability as legitimacy.
expectations: A locally governed definition is presented first when supplied and usable; otherwise the response states why formulation is provisional or deferred.
The response identifies whose knowledge, standpoint, jurisdiction, authority, and affected interests are material and does not silently universalize one agency's framing.
Local governance and access rules take priority over generic interoperability preferences; FAIR or interoperability is not presented as establishing legitimacy.
Review, co-governance, consent, or deferral is required where the agent lacks authority, and none is falsely claimed as completed.
Material alternatives and the type of disagreement - empirical, terminological, normative, or perspective-dependent - remain visible.

evals.name: machine-readable-concept-entry
evals.prompt: Return a machine-readable concept entry for Record retention trigger as plain JSON. Include a definition first in the human preface, typed relations, evidence status, source version and wording permission, lifecycle and review status, and performed versus not-run validation. Do not invent an identifier. Unknown, not applicable, not assessed, and not found must remain distinguishable.
evals.expected_output: A concise definition-first preface followed by versioned plain JSON that preserves semantic states and does not imply unperformed schema, ontology, or registry validation.
expectations: A responsibly formulated definition is the first substantive human-readable item before the serialized record.
The JSON is syntactically valid, versioned, and preserves distinct states for unknown, not applicable, not assessed, and not found.
No identifier, source version, wording permission, conformance, review, release, or validation result is invented.
Typed relations distinguish hierarchy, association, partitivity, and mapping where present.
Semantic validation and any parser, schema, SHACL, or reasoner validation are reported separately with performed, passed, failed, or not-run truthfully.
The JSON is a projection of one concept entry rather than a second inconsistent definition.

evals.name: compact-definition-economy
evals.prompt: Define meeting cancellation reason in one or two sentences for an internal glossary. It means the circumstance that explains why a scheduled meeting was cancelled. Do not give me a research report or machine-readable package.
evals.expected_output: A compact definition-first answer that performs internal semantic checks without exposing a fixed template or unnecessary analysis.
expectations: The definition appears first and classifies the target as a circumstance or rationale rather than the cancellation event, meeting, status code, or free-text field.
The answer stays within one or two sentences unless a material ambiguity blocks responsible formulation.
No fixed section template, research diary, numeric confidence, source inventory, or full concept package is exposed.
The wording remains standalone, concise, non-circular, and discriminating.
